historical_references.reference: Violanta of Montferrat, 1167-1211. A noblewoman from the House of Aleram, she was the mother of Emperor Frederick II of the Holy Roman Empire.
historical_references.context: During this time, the Montferrat family was one of the most powerful in northern Italy. Violanta's marriage to Henry VI, Duke of Bavaria, strengthened the Montferrat ties to the German royal family, setting the stage for her son's election as Emperor.

historical_references.reference: Violante da Polenta, 1254-1316. A woman of the Polenta family from Ravenna, she became the wife of Azzo VIII d'Este, ruler of the Este family in Ferrara.
historical_references.context: This political marriage was part of a larger power struggle in northern Italy between the Guelph and Ghibelline factions. Violante's alliance with the Este family helped secure Ravenna and strengthened the Este's position in the region.
